verdict.rationale: Viam's docs cover each part of the story. Drivers come from the Registry: you name the hardware model in the config and viam-server pulls and initializes the driver automatically. A setup wizard and discovery service handle configuration and get the machine online, and test panels plus the motion service deliver first motion; a tutorial claims motor control in about 2 minutes. Community comments note it needs a Linux/TCP-capable compute device and internet access, which limits scope but does not contradict the claims. missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of the hours-not-weeks timeline, evidence for bring-up of hardware without existing Registry drivers.

support.subject: As a robotics engineer, I can bring up a new robot — drivers, configuration, first motion — in hours rather than weeks

citations.quote: Specify your hardware model and connection details in the config, and viam-server pulls the driver from the Registry and initializes it automatically.
You'll create a machine in the Viam app, install Viam on your compute device, and confirm it's online.
Discovery: Detect available hardware on a machine and suggest component configurations
Drive bases with keyboard controls, move arms to specific positions, or test components directly from Viam's web interface. Debug without deploying code.
Control a motor in 2 minutes: Use Viam to control a motor's speed and direction in just a few steps.
